base.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 2 slot bays are EMPTY; cooling, psus, res are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.
base.source: derived - built from the group roles rather than from a vendor bundle: every bay whose group is `service` or `management` keeps its seat, every `traffic` bay takes a blank. This vendor publishes no base configuration for this chassis, so the library defines one. Where a vendor DOES publish one, follow it instead and say so here.

datasheet.title: Juniper MX10003 Universal Routing Platform datasheet

description: Juniper MX10003 - a 3RU, 2.4 Tbps edge router. Two Routing and Control Boards run side by side across the top; below them two full-width MPCs (JNP10003-LC2103), each with a JNP-MIC1 12xQSFP28 MIC in its left half and six fixed QSFP+ ports with a GM/PTP jack at the right. The rear is two three-high PSM stacks flanking four vertical fan modules (FT 0-3).

gaps.wanted: the DC PSM face (the guide's DC figures are isometric line art; the DC supply is also deeper - 274.3 vs 235.2 mm).
the printed PSM slot labels - the rear drawing's edge legends are not legible in any source, so left-stack-top-down 0-2 / right-stack 3-5 is an assumption.
the position of the two-hole protective earthing bracket on the side rail (M4 studs at 19.1 mm centres per the guide, location not drawn).
a photograph of the rear - only the schematic line drawing g009801 exists in the intake, so rear finish is inferred.

attrs.redundancy-note: n+n - six supply bays. Minimum for NON-redundant operation is 2 for AC high line, 3 for DC and 4 for AC low line; with additional supplies the system provides N+1 and N+N, and n+n is the fully redundant mode where one supply carries the router indefinitely

psus.description: six power supply modules in two three-high rear stacks

attrs.redundancy-note: 1+1 - mx10003 hardware guide, "MX10003 Component Redundancy": the host subsystem is a pair of Routing and Control Boards; with two fitted one is primary and the other backup, the backup takes over if the primary or any part of it fails, and the RCB in slot 0 is primary by default. So the pair is primary/backup and not load-sharing

res.description: Routing and Control Board slots RE0 and RE1

name: mx10003

chassis.note: datasheet-table - 5.21 x 17.6 x 30 in (132.3 x 447 x 762 mm), 3RU; the guide physical table repeats it. Ears NOT MODELLED by convention (the rack face is 19 in / 482.6 mm)

front.note: photo - the frontwtop photograph measured at ~2.95 px/mm across the 447 mm body: RCBs at x 17.0 and 227.4 over rows y 2.0; MPCs at x 14.0 (centred 419.1 in 447), rows y 46.0 and 89.5; positions approximate to ~2 mm. fru-sizes.note: datasheet-table - the guide carries a full FRU dimension table (RCB 202.7 x 42.1, MPC 419.1 x 41.9, MIC 197.3 x 41.9, fan module 62.5 x 126.7, PSU 86.7 face); every component size is vendor-stated

other-faces.note: near-blank by evidence - rail bands estimated; axis conventions per viewer3d.js as the siblings

power.note: datasheet-table - the guide power planning tables: a fully configured chassis at high activity with QSFP28 optics and two JNP-MIC1 draws 1676 W at 25 C (Table 24) and 2110 W at 55 C (Table 25), OUTPUT side; the 90% efficiency column gives the INPUT figures 1862 W and 2344 W. With JNP-MIC1-MACSEC the rows read 1736/1929 W and 2180/2422 W and are not carried. The worked examples sum the same totals from Table 23 (4 fans 80 W + 2 MPCs 1320 W + 2 MICs 160 W + 2 RCBs 116 W = 1676 W; 380 + 1430 + 170 + 130 = 2110 W at 55 C) but describe the router as idle where the tables say high activity, and the 55 C example rounds the input to 2345 W where Table 25 says 2344 W - the vendor is inconsistent with itself, and the tables are what is carried

rear.note: drawing - g009801: three-high PSM stacks at both rear corners and four vertical fan trays between them (FT 0-3). The drawing is schematic, so the stacks are anchored to the vendor PSU and fan module dimensions, not to drawing pixels. PSM slot numbering is not legible in any source - see gaps
